senses.definition: look forward to the probable occurrence of
examples: We were expecting a visit from our relatives
She is looking to a promotion
he is waiting to be drafted

senses.definition: mentally perceptive and responsive
examples: an alert mind
alert to the problems
alive to what is going on
awake to the dangers of her situation
was now awake to the reality of his predicament

senses.definition: not in a state of sleep; completely conscious
examples: lay awake thinking about his new job
still not fully awake

senses.definition: stop sleeping
examples: She woke up to the sound of the alarm clock

senses.definition: a grant made by a law court
examples: he criticized the awarding of compensation by the court

senses.definition: a tangible symbol signifying approval or distinction
examples: an award for bravery

senses.definition: something given for victory or superiority in a contest or competition or for winning a lottery
examples: the prize was a free trip to Europe

senses.definition: give as judged due or on the basis of merit
examples: the referee awarded a free kick to the team
the jury awarded a million dollars to the plaintiff
Funds are granted to qualified researchers

senses.definition: give, especially as an honor or reward
examples: bestow honors and prizes at graduation

senses.definition: (sometimes followed by ‘of’) having or showing knowledge or understanding or realization or perception
examples: was aware of his opponent's hostility
became aware of her surroundings
aware that he had exceeded the speed limit

senses.definition: bearing in mind; attentive to
examples: ever mindful of her health
mindful of his responsibilities
mindful of these criticisms, I shall attempt to justify my action

senses.definition: having knowledge of
examples: he had no awareness of his mistakes
his sudden consciousness of the problem he faced
their intelligence and general knowingness was impressive

senses.definition: state of elementary or undifferentiated consciousness
examples: the crash intruded on his awareness

senses.definition: (of a baseball pitch) on the far side of home plate from the batter
examples: the pitch was away (or wide)
an outside pitch

senses.definition: not present; having left
examples: he's away right now
you must not allow a stranger into the house when your mother is away

senses.definition: used of an opponent's ground
examples: an away game

senses.definition: at a distance in space or time
examples: the boat was 5 miles off (or away)
the party is still 2 weeks off (or away)
away back in the 18th century

senses.definition: freely or at will
examples: fire away!

senses.definition: from a particular thing or place or position (‘forth’ is obsolete)
examples: ran away from the lion
wanted to get away from there
sent the children away to boarding school
the teacher waved the children away from the dead animal
went off to school
they drove off
go forth and preach

senses.definition: from one's possession
examples: he gave out money to the poor
gave away the tickets

senses.definition: in a different direction
examples: turn aside
turn away one's face
glanced away

senses.definition: in or into a proper place (especially for storage or safekeeping)
examples: put the toys away
her jewels are locked away in a safe
filed the letter away

senses.definition: in reserve; not for immediate use
examples: started setting aside money to buy a car
put something by for her old age
has a nest egg tucked away for a rainy day

senses.definition: indicating continuing action; continuously or steadily
examples: he worked away at the project for more than a year
the child kept hammering away as if his life depended on it

senses.definition: out of existence
examples: the music faded away
tried to explain away the affair of the letter
idled the hours away
her fingernails were worn away

senses.definition: out of the way (especially away from one's thoughts)
examples: brush the objections aside
pushed all doubts away

senses.definition: so as to be removed or gotten rid of
examples: cleared the mess away
the rotted wood had to be cut away

senses.definition: a feeling of profound respect for someone or something
examples: the fear of God
the Chinese reverence for the dead
the French treat food with gentle reverence
his respect for the law bordered on veneration

senses.definition: an overwhelming feeling of wonder or admiration
examples: he stared over the edge with a feeling of awe

senses.definition: inspire awe in
examples: The famous professor awed the undergraduates

senses.definition: inspiring awe or admiration or wonder
examples: New York is an amazing city
the Grand Canyon is an awe-inspiring sight
the awesome complexity of the universe
this sea, whose gently awful stirrings seem to speak of some hidden soul beneath
Westminster Hall's awing majesty, so vast, so high, so silent

senses.definition: causing fear or dread or terror
examples: the awful war
an awful risk
dire news
a career or vengeance so direful that London was shocked
the dread presence of the headmaster
polio is no longer the dreaded disease it once was
a dreadful storm
a fearful howling
horrendous explosions shook the city
a terrible curse

senses.definition: exceptionally bad or displeasing
examples: atrocious taste
abominable workmanship
an awful voice
dreadful manners
a painful performance
terrible handwriting
an unspeakable odor came sweeping into the room

senses.definition: extreme in degree or extent or amount or impact
examples: in a frightful hurry
spent a frightful amount of money

senses.definition: inspired by a feeling of fearful wonderment or reverence
examples: awed by the silence
awful worshippers with bowed heads

senses.definition: inspiring awe or admiration or wonder
examples: New York is an amazing city
the Grand Canyon is an awe-inspiring sight
the awesome complexity of the universe
this sea, whose gently awful stirrings seem to speak of some hidden soul beneath
Westminster Hall's awing majesty, so vast, so high, so silent

senses.definition: offensive or even (of persons) malicious
examples: in a nasty mood
a nasty accident
a nasty shock
a nasty smell
a nasty trick to pull
Will he say nasty things at my funeral?

senses.definition: used as intensifiers
examples: terribly interesting
I'm awful sorry

senses.definition: causing inconvenience
examples: they arrived at an awkward time

senses.definition: difficult to handle or manage especially because of shape
examples: an awkward bundle to carry
a load of bunglesome paraphernalia
clumsy wooden shoes
the cello, a rather ungainly instrument for a girl

senses.definition: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
examples: awkward (or embarrassing or difficult) moments in the discussion
an awkward pause followed his remark
a sticky question
in the unenviable position of resorting to an act he had planned to save for the climax of the campaign

senses.definition: lacking grace or skill in manner or movement or performance
examples: an awkward dancer
an awkward gesture
too awkward with a needle to make her own clothes
his clumsy fingers produced an awkward knot

senses.definition: not elegant or graceful in expression
examples: an awkward prose style
a clumsy apology
his cumbersome writing style
if the rumor is true, can anything be more inept than to repeat it now?

senses.definition: socially uncomfortable; unsure and constrained in manner
examples: awkward and reserved at parties
ill at ease among eddies of people he didn't know
was always uneasy with strangers
